newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dlr ends little changed, awaits polls next week.
newsitem.headline: NZ dlr ends little changed, awaits polls next week.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed barely changed on Friday but dealers said there had been reasonable two-way trade in a slightly wider range than earlier in the week.
The currency nudged up a few points at the close to reach US$0.6920/27, a couple of basis points up from its opening level. The Trade-Weighted Index ended at 65.52, up from 65.47.
A Wellington dealer said two opinion polls expected at the start of next week would provide a focus of interest, with the October 12 general election now just six weeks away.

The last poll on August 23 was bad for the governing National Party, which was still easily the strongest party but slipped to 34 percent against a total of 57 percent for the Labour, New Zealand First and Alliance parties.
Dealers said political concerns had been set aside lately by the market, largely because they were outweighed by Eurokiwi and samurai-related buying.

An Auckland trader said more issues were expected as the Northern Hemisphere holiday season drew to an end. "We believe there's a bit of a bottleneck of Euro-issuance to be done when they do return from holidays," he said.
The Kiwi may also take a lead from any movement in the Australian dollar, with rumours in the market of a possible Australian rate cut next week.
In the meantime the Kiwi was seen idling in a 0.6910-35 range.
